hook: An old phone may replace a Raspberry Pi in one maker's project.
hooks: An old phone may replace a Raspberry Pi in one maker's project.
I rooted a cheap phone and used its camera, GPS and storage instead of buying a Pi and extra modules.
The phones sell for about ¥300–500, roughly $45–75 each.
what_happened: The author rooted a Redmi 13C 5G and is testing its camera, storage and GPS in place of a Raspberry Pi and add-on modules.
why_it_matters: The author's listings put a used phone near ¥300–500 against about ¥1,483 for a Pi 4 build with camera, GPS and storage.
the_catch: Finding many matching phones with healthy batteries would take more work.
caption: An old phone may replace a Raspberry Pi in one maker's project, by supplying camera, GPS and storage. Phone or Pi?
alt_text: The slides describe one maker testing a rooted second-hand phone's camera, GPS and storage in place of a Raspberry Pi and add-on modules.
